svg.title: DSpark Training: Kernel Optimizations
svg.desc: Three paths: fused Q/K preparation, mask-aware sparse attention, and on-chip shared-head gradient reduction. The bottom comparison measures attention forward plus backward only.
svg.metadata: {"source":"docs/dspark_attn_kernel_optimization.md","evidence":"docs/assets/dspark-attention-training/benchmark-evidence.json","scope":"Conceptual kernel diagrams; attention F+B timing only, fixed 128K/B7 workload.","routes":[{"name":"Torch Flex","attention_fb_ms":58.52},{"name":"FA4","attention_fb_ms":48.59},{"name":"Interval FA4","attention_fb_ms":30.16},{"name":"cuDNN","attention_fb_ms":21.15},{"name":"Joint GQA","attention_fb_ms":18.12}],"full_attention":true,"block_size":7,"gqa_ratio":4}
svg.text: Fuse preparation. Preplan visibility. Reduce shared-head gradients on chip.
Document isolation is encoded in the mask.
Projection GEMMs and V concat remain separate.
Full tiles need no score predicate.
Partial tiles still execute dense MMA.
Less mask logic inside the main kernel
Hq/Hkv = 32/8 → 4 Q heads per KV head
Group Q heads; no external Q/dO folding.
Measured attention F+B · fixed 128K / B=7 workload
3.23× versus Torch Flex · 14.3% lower latency versus native cuDNN
Timings exclude Q/K preparation, plan construction, external layout conversion and the rest of training.
BF16 tensor boundaries · FP32 accumulation · unchanged visibility and anchor budget
